claim: A chimeric Pfizer/Moderna spike sequence integrated into chromosome 19 of a bladder-cancer patient — 1-in-a-trillion odds of being an anomaly.
oneLiner: A single chimeric sequencing read in one case report is not evidence of vaccine DNA integration.
summary: A case report in a Beall's-list journal describes one chimeric read in cell-free plasma DNA that the authors call integration into chromosome 19. One chimeric read with no orthogonal validation is a sequencing artifact, not integration; the "20/20 bp match" and "1-in-a-trillion" framings misuse statistics; the spike sequence is not unique to the vaccine; and the authors have major conflicts of interest.
bodyMarkdown: See `mrna-vaccine-integration-factcheck.md` in the repo root for the full fact-check.

claim: Ivermectin is a proven cure for COVID-19.
oneLiner: Large randomized trials show no clinically meaningful benefit of ivermectin for COVID-19.
summary: The largest randomized controlled trials (TOGETHER, ACTIV-6, PRINCIPLE) found no clinically meaningful benefit of ivermectin for COVID-19 on hospitalization, recovery time, or mortality. Smaller early-pandemic signals did not hold up on replication; the most widely circulated meta-analysis was withdrawn after fabricated data were identified in an included study.

claim: COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips or tracking devices.
oneLiner: There is no electronic component in any authorized COVID-19 vaccine; the volume alone makes it physically impossible.
summary: Authorized COVID-19 vaccines contain mRNA or viral vector DNA, lipids, salts, and sugars. No integrated circuit small enough to pass through a vaccine needle and remain functional has been demonstrated, and independent chemical analyses of vials across the Pfizer, Moderna, and J&J products have found only the ingredients listed on the FDA fact sheets.

claim: mRNA-vaccinated people "shed" vaccine components and harm unvaccinated people around them.
oneLiner: mRNA vaccines contain no live virus and cannot shed.
summary: Shedding is a property of live-attenuated viral vaccines (e.g. some oral polio formulations). mRNA vaccines contain synthetic mRNA inside lipid nanoparticles — no replicating virus, no viable particle to shed. The claim conflates two unrelated vaccine platforms.

claim: Natural immunity from infection is always stronger and safer than vaccine immunity.
oneLiner: Post-infection immunity is real but comes at the cost of the infection itself; hybrid immunity (infection + vaccination) is generally the strongest.
summary: Studies show infection-derived immunity provides substantial protection against reinfection and severe disease, often comparable to or exceeding primary-series vaccination for the same variant. But that protection only exists after surviving the infection, which carries non-trivial risk of hospitalization, Long COVID, and death. Multiple large cohort studies show the strongest and most durable protection is hybrid immunity (prior infection plus vaccination).
